thread.title_full: Hundreds of animals rescued from 'appalling' conditions at Southern California sanctuary - NewsBreak

author: Jocelyn Fiset
title: Hundreds of animals rescued from 'appalling' conditions at Southern California sanctuary - NewsBreak
text:
By Jocelyn Fiset ,
8 hours ago
A massive rescue operation is underway for hundreds of animals at a San Diego County animal sanctuary after officials served a search warrant at the property on May 1.
More than 550 animals of all kinds were reportedly found living in dangerous conditions at the Villa Chardonnay Sanctuary in Julian.
Officials said many are being treated for injuries and disease tied to severe neglect, and veterinarians have been working around the clock since the first wave of animals came in.
The San Diego Humane Society is calling what they found on the 40-acre property “appalling,” and said it’s one of the largest cases in its 145-year history.
More than 300 cats were rescued from Villa Chardonnay Sanctuary in Julian, Calif. since May 1, 2026. (San Diego Humane Society) “This is one of the largest and most complex rescues our organization has ever undertaken,” said Jace Huggins, Vice President and Chief of Humane Law Enforcement at San Diego Humane Society. “We are currently managing a 40-acre property to stabilize and rescue hundreds of animals who have suffered from significant deficiencies in care and welfare.”
“It truly is appalling,” said Dr. Gary Weitzman, president and CEO at San Diego Humane Society. “There is no question at all about the neglect, at the very least, that occurred out there. I am very happy that these animals have a new chance at life.”
Estimated total number of animals rescued as of May 4, according to animal rescue officials:
Approximately 165 horses and several ponies More than 300 cats (with an estimated 50-100 still on the property) 30 dogs Dozens of other animals, including goats, alpacas, pigs, chickens and more. These animals are now in the care of San Diego Humane Society.
Officials said many of the 350 cats needed immediate medical attention — with some considered very underweight and emaciated.
Pasadena Humane and other California animal welfare organizations were called in to assist the San Diego Humane Society with removing animals from the property, performing medical exams and transport.
Hundreds of dogs, cats rescued in L.A. County in possibly largest U.S. case “The conditions of the animals were heartbreaking, with many suffering from emaciation, contagious diseases, and open wounds as a result of prolonged neglect,” according to Pasadena Humane.
San Diego Humane Society officials said some of the animals were in such critical condition that humane euthanasia was necessary, including four horses, a pony, a bull and one kitten who passed away in care.
Officials said they’ve received nearly 100 submissions from individuals who believe their owned animals were boarded or surrendered at the Villa Chardonnay property, and they’re working to reunite animals with their original owners.
A criminal investigation is underway, but no charges have been filed yet.
Huggins said conditions at Villa Chardonnay have raised concerns for years, and it’s one of the worst cases of animal hoarding they’ve seen.
